statements.quote: I’ll let you know how the eTNS (and the methotrexate rechallenge) goes!
statements.context: Author reports using the Monarch eTNS device for his own ADHD, pausing it for two nights during an autoimmune flare with hemicrania continua and mild ptosis, then restarting it at his wife's urging; he promises a future update on how the eTNS and his methotrexate rechallenge go.
statements.note: Commitment to report on own device use and drug rechallenge in the newsletter; not a world-state forecast. Borderline, logged for recall.

statements.quote: Thanks for joining me on this World Health Day, which is maybe what we call it in the future.
statements.context: Closing line of an essay arguing that the word 'mental' in front of 'health' confuses more than it clarifies and that health should be assessed as ability versus disability; the author suggests the day may be called 'World Health Day' in the future.
statements.note: Half wish, half prediction about renaming the day; hedged with 'maybe'.

statements.quote: It will be hard to explain why making me pay 29 extra dollars to your Pharmacy benefit manager and then paying extra for the drug all over again is in my interest as a plan member.
statements.context: After paying $24.32 cash with a CapitalRx cost-plus card versus a $54.11 insurance copay at a Walgreens-owned Duane Reade, the author says the ERISA 'no gag clause' attestation law will make it hard for plan sponsors (CEOs and CFOs) to justify PBM arrangements that overcharge plan members.
statements.note: Prediction about plan sponsors' position once the gag-clause law applies; paired with the December 31, 2023 effective-date statement.

statements.quote: That law goes into effect for every CEO and every CFO of every company covered by ERISA on December 31, 2023. Buckle up.
statements.context: The author's 'no gag clause' law (his term for the ERISA fiduciary attestation requirement) takes effect for every CEO and CFO of ERISA-covered companies on December 31, 2023; 'Buckle up' implies consequences for employers that keep conventional PBM arrangements. He says most companies are probably in breach of fiduciary duty now.
statements.note: Dated statement of a statutory effective date plus an implied warning of consequences for employers.

statements.quote: I will calculate that for my readers at the end of this quarter, and you can see how I did.
statements.context: In an essay on OKRs (Measure What Matters, John Doerr), the author says he publishes almost every day and commits to calculating and publishing his daily-publication rate for The Frontier Psychiatrists at the end of the current quarter (Q4 2023).
statements.horizon_text: at the end of this quarter
statements.note: Commitment about the newsletter (own organization); CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: I would probably want to set another key result to guide me when I revisit the original goal and its measurement.
statements.context: Author reflects that publishing daily was not an audacious enough OKR key result for the newsletter (he hit it more than 70% of the time) and says he will probably set another key result when he revisits the goal.
statements.horizon_text: when I revisit the original goal
statements.note: Weak stated intention about own newsletter goals; borderline, logged for recall.

statements.quote: The healthcare industry is increasingly focused on value-based care models and consumerism, leading companies to make significant investments that may take longer to materialize into EBITDA.
statements.context: Footnote 2 of a satirical Wizard of Oz parody about private equity in healthcare (the Tin Man as a PE investor). The footnote states that healthcare companies' value-based-care and consumerism investments may take longer to show up in EBITDA, while high valuations and aggressive capital structures leave new issuers little room for error.
statements.note: Unattributed footnote; wording reads like copied ratings-agency text, so attribution is unclear. Main text is satire; the footnote is sincere.

statements.quote: If current trends continue, this downturn will have different implications for PE activity writ large and healthcare private equity specifically.
statements.context: Footnote 3 quotes a Bain report on healthcare private equity: if current trends continue, the downturn (geopolitical uncertainty, inflation, rising rates, bank failures) will affect PE activity and healthcare PE differently from the 2000-01 and 2008-09 recessions. Cited as backing for the satire's 'my margins slipped' line.
statements.note: Quoted third party (Bain report); the author cites it but does not explicitly adopt it. Vague outcome.

statements.quote: If these dynamics result in depressed 2022 EBITDA values for provider businesses, sponsors may look to hold their provider businesses through the downturn, reducing potential provider deal volumes further into 2023.
statements.context: Bain report quoted in footnote 3: healthcare wage inflation and restricted financing may depress 2022 EBITDA for provider businesses, so PE sponsors may hold those assets through the downturn and provider deal volumes may fall further into 2023.
statements.note: Quoted third party (Bain report); conditional forecast, not explicitly adopted by the author.

statements.quote: provider deals dropped nearly 50% from Q3 to Q4, and may continue to impact HCPE deal volumes in 2023.
statements.context: Bain report quoted in footnote 3: the near-50% drop in provider deals from Q3 to Q4 2022 may continue to depress healthcare private equity (HCPE) deal volumes in 2023.
statements.note: Quoted third party (Bain report); not explicitly adopted by the author.

statements.quote: I’m about to hit my 400th post.
statements.context: Short promotional post offering a 50% subscription discount and a drug discount card; the author says the newsletter's 400th post is imminent.
statements.note: Trivial milestone claim about own newsletter; logged for recall.

statements.quote: Neither high turnover of health care personnel nor doubling their wages is a great look for a country with triple the number of elderly people in 2060, but it’s a splash in the pan compared to the graft in the system.
statements.context: Part I of a co-written (with Sanjay Shirke) history of US healthcare payment. Discussing CPT codes, physician burnout and unionization, the author asserts the US will have triple the number of elderly people in 2060 and that labor costs are small next to system graft.
statements.note: Demographic projection stated as fact, embedded in a broader point about healthcare labor costs.

statements.quote: I have a webinar coming up with Al Lewis!
statements.context: Promotional message at the end of Part II of the healthcare payment series: the author announces an upcoming Acacia Clinics x Validation Institute webinar with Al Lewis about employer-sponsored health plans.
statements.note: Event announcement about own organization (Acacia); CONTROL candidate. The next post dates the webinar November 7.

statements.quote: As part of your employer-sponsored health plan, we will discuss how your company can have next-generation psychiatric treatment—with the fancy BRAIN , SAINT , Monarch eTNS , and other treatments you read about here at a lower cost than you pay for care now—with a total of a 150,000 dollar value bet on that claim’s veracity.
statements.context: Promotional message for the Acacia Clinics x Validation Institute webinar with Al Lewis: the author claims employers can get next-generation psychiatric treatments (BRAIN, SAINT, Monarch eTNS) through their health plan at a lower cost than they pay for care now, backed by a $150,000 value bet.
statements.note: Claim about own organization's offering (Acacia); CONTROL candidate. Cost claim backed by a stated $150,000 value bet.

statements.quote: I explained the future of mental healthcare and how the crisis we’re facing can be over, if only we would pay for things that exist now
statements.context: Introducing a five-minute video on the AI-guided future of mental health care, the author claims the mental health crisis can be ended if payers fund treatments that already exist.
statements.note: Conditional claim: the condition is payer behavior, the outcome is the end of the mental health crisis.

statements.quote: I will be hosting a webinar with Al Lewis through the Validation Institute on November 7, here is the link to sign up for that.
statements.context: Author announces he will host a webinar with Al Lewis through the Validation Institute on November 7 (2023) about getting the treatments in his video into an employee benefits plan.
statements.note: Dated event commitment about own activities; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: I will tell more of this story over time because self-disclosure among health professionals ... can de-stigmatize in a way little else can.
statements.context: 400th post; the author discloses his own August 2013 inpatient psychiatric admission at Lenox Hill Hospital while a third-year resident and commits to telling more of the story in future posts.
statements.note: Commitment about future newsletter content (own organization); quote joins across a footnote marker.

statements.quote: Bipolar disorder is a circadian rhythm disorder even more than a mood disorder.
statements.context: Essay arguing that bipolar disorder is fundamentally a circadian rhythm disorder driven by 460nm light input to the suprachiasmatic nucleus; the title and closing line hedge with 'Maybe', and the intro frames it as 'whatever bipolar disorder turns out to be'.
statements.note: Present-tense scientific hypothesis, not a forecast; logged for recall because the author frames it as awaiting resolution.
